s1.syndrome_frame: Episodic hypertension with micturition-related syncope and symptoms of catecholamine excess
salient_findings: Micturition-related episodes of headaches, diaphoresis, palpitations, chest pain, and presyncope
Tachycardia and significant blood pressure lability
Elevated plasma free metanephrine levels and isolated elevation in plasma normetanephrine
Bilateral crackles on pulmonary examination and pink, frothy secretions from endotracheal tube
key_facts: 2-year history of episodic hypertension
Micturition-related syncope
Episodic chest pain, palpitations, and diaphoresis
Tachycardia (112 beats/min) on arrival
Blood pressure 196/120 mmHg on arrival
High-sensitivity troponin T: 936 ng/L, peaked at 1026 ng/L
Plasma free metanephrine levels: isolated elevation in plasma normetanephrine (36 nmol/L)
24-hour urinary metanephrines: isolated normetanephrine elevation (8990 mcg)
Free norepinephrine: 21,685 pg/mL, with normal epinephrine and dopamine levels
Bilateral hilar opacities suggesting acute pulmonary edema on chest radiography
Mildly depressed left ventricular systolic function (EF 40-45%) with hypokinesis of septum and inferolateral wall on transthoracic echocardiogram
1.9 cm × 2.8 cm contrast-enhancing mass in bladder wall with surrounding lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen

shortlist.label: Phaeochromocytoma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Micturition-related symptoms and catecholamine excess with a bladder mass on CT abdomen

shortlist.label: Paraganglioma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to phaeochromocytoma, with episodic hypertension and symptoms of catecholamine excess

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Classic cause of episodic hypertension and catecholamine excess, though less likely given the bladder mass

shortlist.label: Paraganglioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can cause episodic hypertension and catecholamine excess, with a possible link to the bladder mass

shortlist.label: Catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that includes phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma, with symptoms matching the case

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including episodic hypertension, micturition-related syncope, and elevated plasma and urinary normetanephrine levels, are consistent with a catecholamine-secreting tumor. The presence of a 1.9 cm × 2.8 cm contrast-enhancing mass in the bladder wall with surrounding lymphadenopathy on CT abdomen strongly supports the diagnosis of Phaeochromocytoma of the bladder.

rejected.label: Paraganglioma of the bladder
rejected.why: While paraganglioma is a possible diagnosis, the term 'phaeochromocytoma' is often used to describe these tumors when they occur in the bladder, making Phaeochromocytoma of the bladder a more specific and preferred diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: Pheochromocytoma typically refers to a tumor of the adrenal gland, whereas the patient's tumor is located in the bladder.

rejected.label: Paraganglioma
rejected.why: Paraganglioma is a more general term that can refer to tumors in various locations, including the bladder, but it does not specify the location, making Phaeochromocytoma of the bladder a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor
rejected.why: While this is a correct description of the tumor's function, it is not as specific as Phaeochromocytoma of the bladder, which provides more information about the tumor's location and type.
